source.title: GLM-RAG: Graph Language Models for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
source.authors: Maya Arseven; Anette Frank; Béni Egressy; J. Higl; Moritz Plenz

record.tranche_reason: The study varies retriever parameter count and measures retrieval performance, a different measure and setting from the original held-out language-model loss scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper measures retrieval Recall@2 as retriever size varies. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit loss power laws, predict larger-run loss, or optimize parameter/token allocations for compute. Its QA results are not a scaling sweep. The relevant results are the parameter-count retrieval comparisons in Table 20 and the aggregate T5-size ablation in Table 16.
record.test_reason: A graph-RAG method paper whose size ablation scales the pretrained T5 encoder inside its GLM retriever (36M, 110M, 336M encoder parameters). It then measures fine-tuned retrieval Recall@2 on five datasets (Table 20, Fig. 6/12). This is a downstream-task-vs-LM-scale result in a new setting, so it bears weakly on V6 only. No pretraining loss is measured, no law is fitted and nothing is extrapolated. The GNN retrievers swept alongside are not language models.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report that GLM-RAG retrieval improves with base-LM size, both in-domain and out-of-domain. GFM-RAG* shows no gain from more parameters, and GFM-RAG+'s upward trend holds only in-domain. They cite Kaplan et al. as context for transformer scaling and leave larger base LMs (beyond 0.8B) to future work. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws as such.
record.recipe_differences: This is a retriever-capacity sweep evaluated with Recall@2, not a language-model pretraining-loss scaling experiment; no power-law fitting or extrapolation is performed.
record.method_sensitivity: The size trend differs by retriever architecture: GLM-RAG improves across the tested datasets, whereas GFM-RAG* and GFM-RAG+ are often flat or non-monotonic. Dataset also affects the GNN-based size results.

fits_no_version.finding: Capacity-matched GNN retrievers (GFM-RAG*, GFM-RAG+, 8M–476M via hidden dim) show flat or non-monotonic Recall@2. Examples: GFM-RAG+ MultiHopRAG 41.4→38.0→35.3→40.1; GFM-RAG* PubMedQA 35.8→35.1→35.0→36.1. The authors say GFM-RAG+ gains hold only in-domain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter scaling of GNN-based graph retrievers does not yield consistent retrieval gains, unlike transformer/LM-based retrievers.

record.problems: Only three GLM-RAG parameter sizes are tested (36M, 110M, 336M); the authors state experiments reach up to 0.8B parameters but larger base models remain future work. The metric is retrieval Recall@2, not held-out language-model loss, and the paper does not fit or evaluate a predictive scaling law. It reports one run per experiment due to computational constraints, although paired bootstrap significance tests and 95% confidence intervals are provided elsewhere.
record.rows_left_out: The capacity-sweep Recall@5 values in Table 20 and the aggregate T5-size Recall@2/Recall@5 values in Table 16 were left out to keep rows focused on the primary metric and non-duplicated dataset-specific results. Figure 6 and Figure 12 show scaling plots overlapping the tabulated results. The training-data scaling plot in Figure 7 is not extracted here because it is a separate data-quantity ablation rather than the parameter-count sweep recorded in these rows.

untested.parts: Predictability: no law or fit relating recall to size, no extrapolation, and no relation to pretraining loss. Only three sizes spanning about one order of magnitude, all T5 encoders. The scaling ablation uses the 60k subset with one run per size.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuning data scaling (Fig. 7) reports recall, not loss, and fits no power law.

missing.what: Recall@5 for the GLM-RAG size sweep. It is also monotonic on all five datasets, e.g. MultiHopRAG 57.7→66.6→78.1.

Aggregate T5 encoder-size ablation, avg Recall@2 60.4/63.3/64.7 (labelled 60M/220M/770M, i.e. full T5 counts). This is declared in rows_left_out but conflicts in size labelling with Table 20 (36M/110M/336M encoder-only).

record.verdict_notes: Bearing on the scaling-laws claim is weak. This is a method paper's own size ablation: three sizes of a fine-tuned T5 encoder, a retrieval metric, no fitted law. The relation could reasonably be downgraded to uses_without_test/T4 if the project excludes own-method size ablations. Parameter counts differ between Table 16 (full T5: 60M/220M/770M) and Tables 19/20 (encoder-only: 36M/110M/336M); the rows use the latter. Scaling ablations are trained on the 60k subset with a single run each. The bootstrap significance tests (Table 23) compare systems, not sizes.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fits and several-orders-of-magnitude loss trends.
Fitting power laws on small runs and predicting loss on much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures retrieval Recall@2, not language-model loss or a broad set of downstream tasks; it does not fit a predictive scaling law or test performance against pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices, and bends in loss curves.

relationships.condition: GLM-RAG retriever, T5 encoder 36M→110M→336M, fine-tuned on 60k Q-Doc pairs, Recall@2 on HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2Wiki, PubMedQA, MultiHopRAG
relationships.reason: Recall@2 rises monotonically with encoder size on all five datasets (R10-R11, R21-R22, R32-R33, R43-R44, R54-R55). The largest gain is MultiHopRAG at 38.6→59.5; 2Wiki gains only 0.7 at the top size. Trend only, with no predictive fit.
relationships.display_finding: Recall@2 increased monotonically across all five datasets, including MultiHopRAG at 38.6→59.5, while 2Wiki gained only 0.7 at the largest size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GLM-RAG size sweep across HotpotQA, MuSiQue, 2Wiki, PubMedQA, and MultiHopRAG
reader_labels.reason: Recall@2 rises at each of the three tested parameter sizes on all five datasets (R9-R11, R20-R22, R31-R33, R42-R44, R53-R55); no predictive law is fitted.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The GNN-based retrievers show flat, modest, or non-monotonic changes across datasets, including declining scores on some settings, rather than a consistent size trend (R1-R8, R12-R19, R23-R30, R34-R41, R45-R52).
